title: Retry Cap
statement: Implement `solve(failures, cap)`. `failures` is how many times the call failed. `cap` is the maximum number of attempts, including the first. Return `{"attempts": used, "stopped": word}` where used is the minimum of failures+... You attempt min(failures, cap) if failures means failures before success? Define it as: you may try at most `cap` times. You needed `failures` failures and then would have stopped anyway. used = min(failures, cap). `stopped` is `cap` when failures is greater than or equal to cap, else `done`. `cap` less than 1 returns `error`.
hints: used is the minimum of failures and cap.
stopped is cap when you hit the ceiling, else done.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Unbounded retries turn a short outage into a stampede.

editorial: Unbounded retries turn a short outage into a stampede. The cap is the number of attempts, not the number of extra tries after the first. Hitting the cap is a stop the caller can see. Finishing earlier is the done path.
